module purpose: neorv32_cpu_lsu captures a memory access address, control attributes, and write data from addr_i, wdata_i, and ctrl_i, formats a data-bus request on dbus_req_o, tracks pending and fault/alignment state, aligns returning bus data into rdata_o, and reports the captured address, wait status, and error status on mar_o, wait_o, and err_o.

use-case flows.value: a qualified load/store request becoming pending and being issued to the data bus
the current access address captured into the memory-address register and checked for alignment
write-request formatting: access attributes, AMO opcode, store payload, and byte enables prepared for the data bus
the atomic-access lock state held on the data-bus request
aligned and sign- or zero-extended load data returned from dbus_rsp_i.data to rdata_o
wait status and load/store error flags reported from ack, misalignment, bus error, and PMP fault status
address, alignment, request fields, lock, read data, pending state, and latched PMP fault cleared when rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.reasoning: When ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we is asserted, the LSU captures addr_i into mar (line 56), exports it on mar_o (line 68), and uses mar to choose which byte or halfword is returned on loads (lines 162 and 169). Integrity is established because a corrupted address changes both the bus target address (`dbus_req_o.addr <= mar;`, line 67, transport field excluded) and the returned load-data lane selection; availability is established because mar is held after capture until used.

conceptual assets.concept: Store data value for the current memory write
conceptual assets.reasoning: The LSU forms the outgoing write payload from wdata_i according to ctrl_i.ir_funct3: byte stores replicate bits 7 downto 0 (line 94), halfword stores replicate bits 15 downto 0 (line 100), and word stores pass wdata_i unchanged (line 103). Integrity is established because the external data-bus consumer must receive exactly the payload defined by these rules. The only sink is dbus_req_o.data, which is a transport-record field and excluded from reporting, so only the setting inputs survive as structural references.

conceptual assets.concept: Write byte-enable mask for the current memory write
conceptual assets.reasoning: The LSU computes dbus_req_o.ben from addr_i and ctrl_i.ir_funct3: byte writes choose one lane by address bits (lines 95-98), halfword writes choose upper or lower halfword from addr_i(1) (line 101), and word writes enable all bytes (line 104). Integrity is established because the bus consumer must receive the exact lane mask defined by these rules; a wrong mask updates the wrong bytes. dbus_req_o.ben itself is excluded as a transport-record field, so the surviving realization points are the inputs that set the decision.

conceptual assets.concept: Load response data returned to the core
conceptual assets.reasoning: When pending is high, rdata_o is loaded from dbus_rsp_i.data using ctrl_i.ir_funct3 and mar to select byte, halfword, or word and to apply sign or zero extension (lines 159-175). Integrity is established because the core-side consumer must receive exactly the value these rules define; availability is established under the RTL-visible condition `pending = '1'`.

conceptual assets.concept: Access alignment decision for the current memory operation
conceptual assets.reasoning: The LSU computes and stores whether the current access is misaligned from ctrl_i.ir_funct3 and the low bits of addr_i (lines 57-60). That decision suppresses request strobing (`dbus_req_o.stb`, line 209) and raises the misalignment error report bits (lines 203 and 205). Integrity is established because an incorrect decision changes whether the access is issued and whether the module reports it as misaligned; availability is established because the decision is held in misaligned after capture.

The pending register tracks whether an LSU access is in flight: when pending is 0 it copies ctrl_i.lsu_req (line 192), and when pending is 1 it clears on dbus_rsp_i.ack or ctrl_i.cpu_trap (lines 193-194). This state gates lock release (line 144), read-data capture (line 159), and all error outputs (lines 203-206). Integrity is established because corrupting the state breaks request sequencing and reporting; availability is established because the register retains the state until the RTL-visible clear conditions occur.

conceptual assets.concept: Protection-fault status for the current access
conceptual assets.reasoning: The LSU samples pmp_fault_i into pmp_err on each clock edge (line 190), blocks bus request strobing directly when pmp_fault_i is high (line 209), and reports the stored result in err_o(1) and err_o(3) via `(dbus_rsp_i.err or pmp_err)` (lines 204 and 206). Integrity is established because permission-fault suppression and reporting must match this input decision; availability is established because pmp_err stores the sampled status for later reporting.

conceptual assets.concept: Encoded AMO operation for the current atomic access
conceptual assets.reasoning: The amo_encode process maps ctrl_i.ir_funct12(11 downto 7) to the internal amo_cmd code (lines 119-130), and mem_do_reg captures that code into dbus_req_o.amoop (line 90). Integrity is established because the external bus consumer must receive exactly the AMO opcode selected by these rules. dbus_req_o.amoop is a transport-record field and excluded from reporting, so the internal computation and its setting input are the eligible realization points.

The bus_lock process asserts the lock bit when `ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we = '1'`, `ctrl_i.lsu_amo = '1'`, and `ctrl_i.ir_funct12(8) = '0'` (lines 142-143), and clears it when pending becomes 0 (lines 144-145). Integrity is established because an atomic sequence depends on that lock state following exactly these conditions. The stored/exported value itself is only dbus_req_o.lock, a transport-record field excluded from reporting, so only the setting input that requests the lock is listed here.

err_o(0..3) reports four distinct access faults: pending load misaligned (line 203), pending load bus/PMP fault (line 204), pending store misaligned (line 205), and pending store bus/PMP fault (line 206). Integrity is established because the consumer of err_o must receive the exact classification produced by these expressions; availability is established whenever the corresponding pending-and-fault conditions hold.

The module reports wait_o directly as `not dbus_rsp_i.ack` (line 200). Integrity is established because the consumer must observe the exact completion/wait status derived from the response acknowledge; availability is established whenever dbus_rsp_i.ack is driven.
